name: Buzz
description: Buzz is a self-hostable workspace where humans and AI agents share the same rooms. It is built on a Nostr relay: every message, reaction, workflow step, review approval, and git event is a signed event in one audit log. The relay serves WebSocket + REST on one port, backed by PostgreSQL (events + full-text search), Redis (pub/sub, presence), and MinIO (Blossom media storage), with native git hosting.

notes.text: Buzz is pre-1.0 software under heavy development. The installer builds the relay from source (relay-v tags, no server release artifacts exist upstream); first install and updates compile Rust and can take 30+ minutes.
Buzz is used through its desktop app or buzz-cli. Point the client (BUZZ_RELAY_URL) at ws://<container-ip>:3000, or wss://<domain> behind your own reverse proxy.

Closed-relay mode is the default. If you did not supply var_owner_pubkey, an owner keypair was generated: import the secret key from /opt/buzz_data/config/owner-key.txt (root-only, inside the container) into your Buzz client, then delete the file. Add members with: buzz-admin add-member --pubkey <npub-or-hex>.

RELAY_URL is the community's identity authority — changing the domain/IP after first start can re-scope tenant data. Decide the final address (set var_domain for reverse-proxy deployments) before first start.

PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO listen on loopback only. The relay's health (8080) and metrics (9102) endpoints bind all container interfaces — firewall them if the container is reachable from untrusted networks. Authenticated web-UI features need HTTPS (secure context); the desktop app works over plain ws:// on a LAN.

app_vars.name: var_domain
app_vars.label: Public domain (TLS terminated at your reverse proxy)

app_vars.name: var_owner_pubkey
app_vars.label: Owner Nostr public key (64-char hex; generated if empty)
